memory_update.text: Tungsten/APT/WF6 is the highest-coherence relationship cluster in this chunk: KMT maps to cemented carbide/tooling demand for APT, ALM maps to non-China upstream tungsten optionality, and APD/LIN are reference specialty-gas anchors requiring direct WF6 proof.

APD and LIN should not yet be treated as proven WF6 bottleneck beneficiaries from the provided evidence because the external tungsten casefile names Stella Chemifa, Daikin, and SK Materials/SK Specialty as primary WF6 suppliers; APD/LIN require independent product/capacity verification.

MKSI and UCTT remain underfollowed second-order semiconductor subsystem candidates, but their relationship to WF6 scarcity or HBM/advanced-packaging growth is inference-heavy until filings show material gas-delivery, vacuum, exhaust, or advanced-packaging revenue sensitivity.

POWL and EME map to the AI data-center power and execution bottleneck lane: POWL through switchgear/power distribution and EME through mechanical/electrical project execution. Both need data-center-specific backlog and margin proof.
NVDA and VRT should remain reference anchors rather than underfollowed candidates: NVDA anchors AI compute demand and VRT anchors visible data-center power/cooling infrastructure demand.
LEU is the clearest reference anchor for the nuclear fuel/HALEU lane; BWXT is a second-order nuclear component and fuel-cycle candidate that requires proof of HALEU or fuel-cycle materiality.

This chunk still lacks market-pricing checks: current market caps, analyst coverage, liquidity, valuation, recent performance, and short interest were not verified in this layer and should not be inferred.

Sulphur/sulphuric acid is strongly evidenced as a New Hotspots supply shock, but this specific candidate chunk contains no mapped public-company beneficiaries for that lane; keep as a coverage gap for later Layer 2B chunks.

summary: Mapped the candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships for the New Hotspots funnel. The strongest internally coherent lane is tungsten/APT/WF6 because the external casefile frames APT as a shared chokepoint across semiconductor WF6, cemented carbide tooling, and defense-grade tungsten qualification. APD and LIN should be retained as reference specialty-gas anchors, but the provided external evidence more directly highlights Japanese and Korean WF6 suppliers, so APD/LIN need direct product and capacity verification before being treated as investable bottleneck exposures. KMT and ALM are the more underfollowed U.S./North America public-market mappings for tungsten pressure, with KMT tied to carbide/tooling margin mechanics and ALM tied to non-China upstream tungsten optionality. AI data-center power names remain a separate lane: NVDA and VRT are reference demand/context anchors, while POWL and EME are second-order bottleneck candidates needing backlog and customer-mix proof. Nuclear fuel remains policy-linked through LEU as reference anchor and BWXT as second-order nuclear component/fuel-cycle exposure. MKSI and UCTT are plausible second-order semiconductor subsystem names, but their relationship to WF6/HBM is currently inference-heavy and requires filings or customer evidence.
